sections.html:
Hanover lies about 12 miles up the road from Richmond and about 90 miles below Washington, D.C. The seat is Hanover Courthouse, Ashland is the only incorporated town, and Mechanicsville is the largest census-designated place. Older farmhouses and village homes near Ashland and the courthouse mix with postwar subdivisions around Mechanicsville, so age and condition vary a lot from one road to the next.

With 82 percent of occupied homes lived in by their owners, most sellers here are individual homeowners rather than landlords.

Hanover has an elected Commissioner of the Revenue, an elected Treasurer and a Clerk of the Circuit Court. Think of three desks. The assessing office puts a number on your house, the Treasurer mails the bill and takes the check, and the Clerk files the deed once you sell. Call the Treasurer and the assessing office for current installment dates and rates before you rely on any date you have read elsewhere.

Questions worth asking on that call:

  • What is the balance on my parcel, and does it include penalty or interest?
  • Which installment is next, and when does the penalty start?
  • By what date must an appeal of this year's value be filed?
  • If we close after a bill is mailed, can it be reissued in the buyer's name?

sections.h2: How a Virginia assessment appeal works
sections.html:
The local board of equalization assumes the assessor got it right, which leaves the proving to you. To prevail, show with a preponderance of the evidence that the house is carried above fair market value, or that the assessment is uneven and set against accepted appraisal practice.

Homes with fewer than four units come with extra protections. The assessing officer owes you written notice, and a written request gets you the assessment records within 15 days. Evidence has limits too: sales up to December 31 before the effective date count if they reach the board by the locality's deadline, and later-published studies do not.

A strong file holds recent comparable sales, photos of defects and proof of factual errors, wrong square footage being the classic one. The statute treats mistakes of fact, computation errors included, as a departure from accepted practice. See the rule at Virginia Code 58.1-3379.

sections.h2: When a house sells after the bill is mailed
sections.html:
Say the deed changes hands just after bills are mailed. The Treasurer may void the old owner's copy and send a new one to the buyer, and if the buyer pays within two weeks of that reissued notice, no penalty can be added to that assessment.

A late penalty on real estate tops out at 10 percent of the tax past due, interest is limited to 10 percent a year during the first year (a different ceiling follows), and collection fees a locality has contracted for can reach 20 percent of the delinquent amount. Hanover's own numbers come from county ordinance, which the Treasurer can quote.

Recording a deed costs money separately. The grantor's tax is 50 cents on every $500 of value, billed to the seller unless the contract puts it on the buyer. Before a deed can be recorded the Clerk has to certify payment, and the proceeds are shared by the state and the locality. See Virginia Code 58.1-802.

On settlement day any unpaid real estate tax also comes out of your proceeds, so ask the Treasurer for a payoff quote in advance and avoid a shock on the statement.

sections.h2: What to have ready for a sale
sections.html:
Hanover sellers can save a week or more by pulling paperwork before a contract arrives. Keep the latest assessment notice, your most recent tax bills with their account numbers and, for an inherited house, the deed or will and any court order naming the person who can sign. Gather any receipts for roof, septic or drainage work as well, since inspectors in a county with both old farm properties and postwar subdivisions tend to dig into those systems.

Interstates 95 and 295 cross the county, and many residents commute toward Richmond, so buyers will ask about drive times and which road your street connects to. If you can, line up three phone calls in one afternoon: the Treasurer for a balance, the assessing office for the appeal deadline and the school division if a buyer has asked about attendance zones. The answers tend to shape both your asking price and your closing date.

1. Confirm the balance and penalty with the Treasurer.
  2. Decide whether this year's value is worth challenging, and if so, collect comparable sales and photos now, since the board accepts only evidence that reaches it by the locality's deadline.
  3. Ask whether any bill already mailed will need to be reissued after closing.
  4. Choose a closing agent and share the payoff and any deed-tax questions in writing.
  5. Once the deed is recorded, ask the Treasurer to confirm the account is paid.

Hanover's mix of rural lots and subdivision homes means the time to sell can swing widely. A neat lot near Ashland or Mechanicsville may draw several showings in a week, while a farmhouse down a country road may wait. Price with that in mind, and tell your agent or buyer about any known issue with a well, septic system or fence line before the inspection does.

A cash sale compresses that list, since there is no lender to wait on, but the tax and the deed levy are handled the same way.

sections.h2: If your tax bill is behind
sections.html:
Behind on tax? You have three realistic routes. Pay from the sale proceeds, ask the Treasurer about an extension or payment plan, or sell to someone who will take the house as it is. A locality may grant extensions of up to 90 days by resolution when good cause exists. A taxpayer who misses a deadline because of a death or a documented medical impairment is presumed to be without fault if payment comes within 30 days.

An assessment under administrative appeal also gets breathing room. An appeal filed within 90 days of the assessment shields the bill from delinquency while the case is open and for 30 days after the final ruling.

A lot of Hanover sales start with a home left vacant after a death, or an aging place needing major repairs. Get the payoff first. Then the person with legal authority to sell should collect the deed and court papers a title company will want.

Cash Home Buyers will tour the house in whatever shape it is in and explain how any tax balance gets cleared when you close. A written cash offer carries no obligation, so you can compare it with other options at your own pace. Buyers also ask which high school a house feeds, so keep the address ready for the school division's attendance lookup.

faqs.q: Who sends the real estate tax bill in Hanover County, Virginia?
faqs.a: The county Treasurer sends and collects the bill. The Commissioner of the Revenue and the assessing office handle values.

faqs.q: What is the Hanover County property tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Call the assessing office for this year's deadline. Under Virginia law the owner must show the value is too high or not uniform.

faqs.q: Can penalties on Hanover County property tax be waived?
faqs.a: Virginia law bars penalty and interest when the failure was not the taxpayer's fault, including certain postal errors, and presumes no fault after a death or medical impairment when payment follows within 30 days. The Treasurer decides fault for late payments.

faqs.q: Who pays the Virginia deed tax when selling a house in Hanover County?
faqs.a: The seller, as grantor, pays the state grantor tax of 50 cents per $500 unless the contract assigns some of it to the buyer. The Clerk of the Circuit Court collects it at recording.
Yes. The 2020 census shows 82.0 percent of occupied housing units owner-occupied and 18.0 percent rented, out of 43,184 housing units.
